**2026-11-23.** A patch release. **A flow can record the exact message each outbound hop sent.**
Every outbound emission binds the instance variable `sent`, holding the body as the governing
codec validated and sealed it, with its content type, destination and outbox key. A later BPMN
step reads it, so a flow's auditing is visible in the flow. No `q:` namespace, migration, archive
or snapshot format change. A 0.8.4 deployment upgrades by changing the image.

## Before you upgrade

- **`sent` is now a reserved variable name.** Each outbound emission overwrites it. A flow that
  used a variable called `sent` for something else should rename it.
- **Sends on timer-resumed steps are now validated and sealed.** On a step a timer fire resumed
  (a timer catch or boundary, a `<q:retry>` re-drive, the tail after `<q:reply continue="true">`),
  or one a channel-call failure resumed (its timeout or a poisoned delivery), 0.8.4 looked the
  outbound channel up under an empty module key. A `<q:send channel>` that did not state its own
  `codec` therefore went out unvalidated and **unsealed**. It is now held to the channel's codec
  and sealed like every other send. A flow that relied on the gap fails that step with
  `SUTRA.OUTBOUND.VALIDATION_REJECT`, or `SUTRA.OUTBOUND.SEAL_FAILED`.
- **Sealing runs at the emitting node,** not when the step is committed. Apart from the fix above,
  the bytes that go out are the same, and so is a refusal: a contract or seal failure fails the
  step with `SUTRA.OUTBOUND.VALIDATION_REJECT` or `SUTRA.OUTBOUND.SEAL_FAILED`, and nothing is
  sent.
- **The outbox key is minted when the message is emitted.** It is the same kind of key as before
  (a random UUID) and reaches the wire unchanged.

## Recording what was sent

`sent` is bound after a `<q:send>` (a send task, a message throw event, or a task carrying one),
a `<q:reply>` with a destination, and a channel-call request:

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| `body` | the body as text: the sealed bytes, envelope, header and signature included |
| `bodyBase64` | the same bytes as base64, only when they are not valid UTF-8 |
| `contentType` | the declared content type, or `null` |
| `destination` | the resolved destination URI |
| `outboxKey` | the idempotency key the outbox row and the wire carry |
| `mode` | `native`, `cloudevent-binary`, `cloudevent-structured` or `match-inbound` |
| `node`, `kind` | the emitting node, and `send`, `reply` or `call` |
| `headers` | the `<q:header>` values |

A data task straight after the send can store it:

```xml
<bpmn:dataObject id="doSent" name="sent"/>
<bpmn:dataStoreReference id="refHop" dataStoreRef="hops">
  <bpmn:extensionElements><q:store key="sent.outboxKey"/></bpmn:extensionElements>
</bpmn:dataStoreReference>
<bpmn:sendTask id="SendRequest">
  <bpmn:extensionElements><q:send channel="peer-out"/></bpmn:extensionElements>
</bpmn:sendTask>
<bpmn:serviceTask id="RecordSent" name="Record what was sent">
  <bpmn:dataOutputAssociation>
    <bpmn:sourceRef>doSent</bpmn:sourceRef>
    <bpmn:targetRef>refHop</bpmn:targetRef>
  </bpmn:dataOutputAssociation>
</bpmn:serviceTask>
<bpmn:sequenceFlow id="toRecord" sourceRef="SendRequest" targetRef="RecordSent"/>
```

Read `sent` in the step directly after the send, since the next emission overwrites it. In the
CloudEvent modes `sent.body` is the body before the envelope is added: `binary` adds the attributes
as headers when the message is delivered, and `structured` wraps the body in a JSON envelope whose
`time` is the delivery instant. A synchronous `<q:reply>` (one with no destination) is rendered
after the flow has finished, so no step can read it.

**Masking.** If a process declares any `sensitive` variable, or an instance holds any redaction
companion (`<v>.redacted`), the engine also stores `sent.redacted`, with the body and every header
value replaced by `[REDACTED]`. Audit snapshots and the inspect API show that copy, and `sent` is
encrypted at rest. The flow itself still reads the real bytes.

**Cost.** Each emission copies its body into a variable once, plus base64 for a binary body. Because
each send overwrites `sent`, an instance holds at most one body this way, and it is persisted with
the instance if the instance parks.

Embedders: `TokenExecutor::builder().with_outbound_seal_seam(…)` wires the new
`OutboundSealSeam`. An executor built without one leaves sealing to the commit, as before, and
its `sent.body` shows the body before sealing.
